changelog: v42e has three changes. (1) The 'Config Check' row no longer shows a trailing number ('ok 1788489150') -- the 10-digit suffix was the check's internal timestamp and only looked like an error; the row now reads ok / restored / error / waiting. (2) The 'Cytech Boot Status' guard (flags 5+ HA restarts in 24h, emailing Cytech and showing a notification) used jargon on the row: state RESTART_STORM, messages about a 'restart loop'. It now reports REPEATED_RESTARTS with plain English: 'The unit restarted N times in the last 24h (first at HH:MM:SS local). Repeated restarts usually mean a problem -- please contact Cytech Support.', and the popup/email say 'Repeated restarts detected'. The id cytech_alert_boot_storm is unchanged. (3) The ROOT CAUSE of the v42c/v42d saga is fixed: GitHub's raw CDN caches each file URL for 5 minutes and the cache key is the URL itself (a query string does NOT bypass it -- verified 2026-09-04), so a device checking or updating within ~5 minutes of a release could be served the PREVIOUS version's file with NO error. That is what v42c did: the unit auto-applied and wrote 'v42c' while keeping the v42b package bytes, and then could never re-apply because it considered itself up to date -- an unfixable state that needed a re-release. From this release, every file is downloaded from a per-version git tag URL (this release is tagged 42e), which no device has ever fetched and therefore can never be cached, so an update can never silently halfapply again. v42d (the re-release attempted for the v42c situation) was itself caught by the stale CDN while being offered and is superseded by this release. Everything below is the v42c story, for units jumping from older versions: v42c made the 'Config Check' row stop showing 'unknown' for up to 4 hours after an update restart -- the runtime integrity check now also runs right after every core start (boot AND update restarts), so the row shows its real result (ok / restored / error) within minutes, and before the first run ever it reads 'waiting' instead of HA's error-lookalike 'unknown'. v42b fixed the row showing 'Entity not found' because Home Assistant pins an entity_id in its entity registry the first time a unique_id is seen -- renaming a sensor does not move a registered entity_id, so the sensor's unique_id was changed and every unit registers fresh as sensor.cytech_integrity_status (the id the row references); v42a was the earlier rename-only attempt that couldn't heal already-registered units. Units coming from v39 or older also get v42/v41/v40 below. v42 makes a corrupted configuration.yaml self-healing, and not just at boot: the system keeps a rolling known-good snapshot of configuration.yaml (refreshed after every clean check -- at boot and every 4 hours while running), and if the live file is ever found corrupt it is replaced by the snapshot with the broken copy saved as configuration.yaml.corrupt.<timestamp>, HA restarts (runtime corruption is repaired the same day it happens, before the next update's restart could land the system in HA recovery mode), and the integrity alert says so. Two safety properties: the snapshot is only refreshed after the configuration actually parsed clean, so a corrupted state can never be snapshotted as 'good'; and no restore happens unless the snapshot itself parses, so there is no restore loop. Integrity alerts are now also emailed (support@cytech.biz always, plus the owner's registered address per the v41 rule), and the System Health dashboard shows a Config Check row with the last running check result. For v39 or older, v42c also carries v40 and v41: the owner's address field is 'My Email for Alerts', a Register press always reports its status on screen (empty field: 'Enter your email first, then press Register.'), a successful Register sends ONE confirmation mail To: the owner Cc: support@cytech.biz, alerts ALWAYS go to support@cytech.biz with the owner's registered address copied automatically (no Cytech/Me/Both selector), and units with mail configured but no owner registered yet show a small non-blocking hint. Nothing is lost if the owner never registers: support@cytech.biz always receives every alert.
